newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese depositing less money in banks - survey.
newsitem.headline: Chinese depositing less money in banks - survey.

text.p: A central bank survey has showed that Chinese deposited less money in banks from March to May and were using funds to buy bonds, the China Securities said on Wednesday.

The survey by the People's Bank of China showed that 34.5 percent of respondents chose to put their money in long-term fixed deposits from March to May, down by about one percentage point compared with a previous survey for the three months to February, it said.
The rate was down by 4.5 percentage points compared with the year-ago period, it said.
The decline in the growth of deposits did not indicate a major change in spending but rather a redisposal of financial assets following two cuts in interest rates last year, it said.
A survey in the capital, Beijing, showed large amounts of cash were being held by residents in the city, particularly stock investors, the Financial News said.
In May, cash held by Beijing residents showed a growth of 45 billion yuan from the beginning of the year, the newspaper said.

At end of June, stock trading accounts opened by Beijing residents reached 890,000, and some 6.29 billion yuan flowed into the stock market and out of bank deposits. In January to May, issue of state debts and corporate bonds caused 14 billion yuan to flow out of bank deposits, it said.
In addition, the postage stamp and coin markets are gradually becoming new investment sectors for residents, the newspaper said but gave no details.
China cut interest rates in May and August last year.
